passages.original: Pauli epistolarum varius ordo, 313. Repetitio in epistola, non erat supperflux , 110 Paulus quatuor modis scribit Romanis, 25. Quibus de causis scripserit ad Cornthios? 111. Ante hanc epistolam aliam tisdem scripserat, ibid., 128. Cur secundam ad Corinthios scripserit epistolam? 169. Scripsit ad Ephesios de urbis Romæ custodia, 251. Cur ad Collossenses scripserit? 263.Et Thessalonicensibus? 275, 276. Et ad Timothæm?. 305 Et scripserit ad Philemonem, 317.
passages.english: The varied order of Paul's epistles, 313. The repetition in the epistle was not superfluous, 110. Paul writes to the Romans in four ways, 25. For what reasons did he write to the Corinthians? 111. Before this epistle he had written another to the same [people], ibid., 128. Why did he write the second epistle to the Corinthians? 169. He wrote to the Ephesians from his custody in the city of Rome, 251. Why did he write to the Colossians? 263. And to the Thessalonians? 275, 276. And to Timothy? 305. And [why] he wrote to Philemon, 317.
passages.notes: This is an index of subjects with page references, not a hymn; the work attribution appears mismatched. Scanning errors corrected: 'supperflux' read as 'superflua', 'Cornthios' as 'Corinthios', 'tisdem' as 'iisdem', 'Collossenses' as 'Colossenses', 'Timothæm' as 'Timotheum'. 'De urbis Romæ custodia' is taken to mean Paul's custody (imprisonment) in Rome; it could also be read as 'about the guarding of the city of Rome'.
